answer: Each identity registers in the lagoon pool and books one jetty berth for a synchronous shift, posting a 50-credit bond plus a 30-credit fee. A rotating pearl auditor checks attendance and output; absence or a key mismatch burns the bond. Berths are scarce: the k-th fake pays 80+2(k-1) credits, so 1,000 fakes lock 1,079,000 credits, with no discount or shift reuse. A rented attendance ring fails: the pearl seal binds output to its key, so a stand-in mismatches and burns the bond. An honest agent books one berth, pays 30 once, and recovers its 50 bond.
